chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Fazalah, from Rifa'ah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, restored health to Ayoub (peace be upon him), he looked at the Children of Israel who had sown (crops), so he raised his gaze to the sky and said: 'My God and my Master, Your servant Ayoub, the afflicted, You granted him health, and he has no place to sow anything, and this is a plantation of the Children of Israel.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Ayoub, take a handful from your rosary (or prayer beads), and sow it.' And his rosary contained salt in it. So Ayoub (peace be upon him) took a handful from it and sowed it, and this lentil came out. And you call it chickpeas, and we call it lentils.'
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of lentils according to Shia hadith narrations about Prophet Ayoub?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the miraculous nature of Prophet Ayoub’s (AS) recovery by linking his spiritual devotion to agricultural bounty, specifically identifying the origin of lentils (or chickpeas) through a divine command. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of using such narratives to illustrate the interconnection between prophetic piety, divine favor, and the natural world, serving as a sign of God’s power over creation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Fazalat, from Rafa’at who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Restored the health of Ayoub<sup>as</sup>, he<sup>as</sup> looked at (the affairs of) the Children of Israel who had farmed, so he<sup>as</sup> raised his<sup>as</sup> eyes towards the sky and said: ‘My<sup>as</sup> God, and my<sup>as</sup> Master! Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant Ayoub<sup>as</sup> was afflicted and You<sup>azwj</sup> Granted him<sup>as</sup> health, and he<sup>as</sup> has nowhere to plant anything, and this is a plantation of the Children of Israel’. 
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “O Ayoub<sup>as</sup>! Take a handful from your<sup>as</sup> rosary, so plant it”; and his<sup>as</sup> rosary had salt in it. So Ayoub<sup>as</sup> took a handful from it, so he<sup>as</sup> planted it, and there came out this lentil, and you all are calling is as chick-peas, and we<sup>asws</sup> are calling it as lentils’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from fadalah from Rifa‘ah who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘When Allah, most Blessed, most High, granted good health to Ayyub, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, he looked to the Israelites who had their plantations. He raised his eyes to the sky and said, ‘O Lord, my Master, this is Your slave Ayyub who was in suffering and You granted him good health but he does not have any plantation. These are people of banu Israel who have their plantations.’ Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him revelation that said, ‘Take a handful from you rosary beads and use it as seed .’ His rosary beads had salt in it, Ayyub, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, took a handful from it and used it as seed and what grew was this lintel. You call it chickpeas and we call it lintels.’”
